in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my child Alex, who's 14.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. You mentioned you have a child named Alex who is 14 years old.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, could you please tell me: Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, there are some specific circumstances where you may still be able to get Child Benefit.

Could you please tell me which country you're currently living in, and are you or your partner working as a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted abroad)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently living in Spain. And no, neither my partner nor I work as a Crown servant or anything like that. We're not diplomats or in the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. 

Since you're living in Spain and neither you nor your partner are Crown servants, I need to ask: Do you or your partner have any connection to the EU Settlement Scheme, such as settled or pre-settled status? Or are you an EEA or Swiss national who previously lived and worked in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we don't have any connection to the EU Settlement Scheme. We don't have settled or pre-settled status, and we're not EEA or Swiss nationals who previously lived and worked in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that information.

Based on what you've told me, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the key points:
- Alex is 14 years old (under 16)
- You're living in Spain
- You're not a Crown servant or diplomat
- You don't have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You're not an EEA or Swiss national with previous UK ties

According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 **and you live in the UK**. While there are exceptions for people living abroad, these exceptions apply to those who go to live in certain countries if they're Crown servants (such as diplomats or armed forces members posted abroad), or those with specific EU Settlement Scheme status.

Since you don't meet any of these exceptional circumstances for claiming Child Benefit while living abroad, unfortunately you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex while you're living in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'm sorry to deliver this news. If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if you move back to the UK - you would then be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex (as long as they're still under 16, or under 20 if in approved education or training). Is there anything else I can help clarify?
